chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah will forgive every sin on the Day of Judgement except the dower of a woman, and the one who usurps the wages of an employee, and the one who sells a free person'.

key_terms.حُرّاً: A free person (as opposed to a slave)
key_terms.مَهْرَ: Dower or dowry given to a wife

ai.seo_question: What are the three sins that Allah does not forgive on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies three specific rights of people (Huquq al-Nas) that remain unforgiven even if the sinner repents for other sins, underscoring the necessity of settling debts with individuals before divine judgment. The inclusion of 'selling a free person' highlights the violation of human dignity and freedom, while usurping a laborer's wages emphasizes economic justice in daily transactions. This serves as a critical reminder in Shia jurisprudence that interpersonal rights require direct restitution, unlike ritual sins which may be forgiven solely through divine mercy.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Forgive every sin on the Day of Judgement except the dower of a woman, and the one who usurps the wages of an employee, and the one who sells a free person’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Allah forgives every sin on the Day of Judgment except non-payment of mahr (dower), usurpation of wages and selling free people.’”
